reviews.body:
Thanks for putting this together to address #741. The lifecycle guard predicate (`lifecycleState == null || lifecycleState == ui.AppLifecycleState.resumed`) is a good direction and keeps public APIs unchanged, but a few issues need to be addressed before approval (see inline comments):

1. **Breaking:** Gating capture only in `ScreenshotCapturer` leaves `ChangeDetector` running while inactive/paused, burning its forced-tick retry budget and stranding static screens unrecorded after returning to `resumed`.
2. **Concern:** `_captureScreenshot()` stops re-checking lifecycle state after `endOfFrame`, leaving `toByteData()`, `captureNativeScreenshots()`, and `currentPicture.toImage()` unguarded if the app leaves the foreground mid-capture.
3. **Concern:** The new tests leave the post-`getSessionReplayState` guard (line 665), non-`inactive` states (`paused`/`hidden`/`detached`), and Test 2's pre-drop progress assertion uncovered.

**Question:** Per [AI_POLICY.md](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-flutter/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md), external contributors are expected to personally review and own submitted code and describe end-to-end verification. Since this PR currently lists `Autonomy: Fully autonomous` with `"I reviewed the submitted code"` unchecked, could you confirm you've reviewed the changes yourself and let us know whether this was verified on an Android device/emulator (especially Android 15 with Impeller OpenGL ES as in #741) or only via widget tests? The answer affects acceptance under `AI_POLICY.md`.

AI-assisted review.

Thanks for the follow-up commits and for updating the PR description!

The earlier `ChangeDetector` background-ticking issue ([discussion_r4673401699](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-flutter/pull/746#discussion_r4673401699)) is now resolved, and formatting, analysis, and the updated tests pass cleanly. However, verifying the new lifecycle observer turned up two introduced **Breaking** regressions in `posthog_widget.dart` (posted inline below), along with remaining follow-ups replied directly on the open threads for `_captureScreenshot()` ([discussion_r4673401717](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-flutter/pull/746#discussion_r4673401717)) and test coverage ([discussion_r4673401725](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-flutter/pull/746#discussion_r4673401725)).

**Question:** Since this hasn't been verified on an Android 15 Impeller GLES device/emulator yet, should we keep `Fixes #741` (which auto-closes `#741` on merge) or change it to `Relates to #741` until confirmed on hardware — and have you checked whether `buildOcclusionPlaceholder()`'s `picture.toImage()` + `toByteData()` (`screenshot_capturer.dart:613, 625`) is safe under Impeller GLES while the Flutter host Activity is paused/stopped under a native screen? The answer determines whether on-device verification or softening the closing keyword is needed before merge.

AI-assisted review.

review_comments.body:
**Concern:** Thanks for adding the guards at lines 770, 870, 902, and 926. There are still a few post-await gaps in `_captureScreenshot()` (`posthog_flutter/lib/src/replay/screenshot/screenshot_capturer.dart`) where a cancelled or backgrounded capture can still run raster-thread work or emit a misleading debug log:

1. **Revealed platform-view compositing loop (lines 878 and 884–889):** After `await _nativeCommunicator.captureNativeScreenshots(specs)` (up to 5s await), line 878 checks only `if (_cancelled)` (not `!_canCaptureInCurrentLifecycle`), and the `for` loop at lines 884–889 checks **neither** `_cancelled` **nor** `!_canCaptureInCurrentLifecycle` before each `await _compositeRevealedView(...)` → `ui.decodeImageFromPixels(...)` (line 481), which uploads pixels on the raster/GPU thread.
2. **Before `currentPicture.toImage` (line 902):** Checks `if (!_canCaptureInCurrentLifecycle)` without `_cancelled`, so cancelling during the platform-view loop can still run `currentPicture.toImage(imageWidth, imageHeight)` at line 906.
3. **After `renderObject.toImage` / `_getImageBytes` (lines 743, 770–795, 909, 929):** Lines 743, 776, 909, and 929 check only `_cancelled`. When `!_canCaptureInCurrentLifecycle` flips without `_cancelled` (e.g. direct `ScreenshotCapturer` usage or once lifecycle cancellation is decoupled from `_cancelled` for occlusion placeholders), line 758 still allocates a `PictureRecorder`, line 770 evaluates to `null`, and line 786 logs the misleading `'Error: Failed to convert image byte data to Uint8List.'` in debug builds (`kDebugMode`).

**Recommendation:** Consider extracting a single helper (paired with the capture-token fix on `posthog_widget.dart`), e.g.:
```dart
bool _shouldAbortCapture(int token) =>
    _cancelled || token != _captureToken || !_canCaptureInCurrentLifecycle;
```
and checking it consistently at lines 665, 718, 743 (before allocating `PictureRecorder` / calling `_getImageBytes`, avoiding the line 786 false error log), 776, 870, 878, inside the `for` loop at line 884 before `_compositeRevealedView`, 902, 909, and 929.

AI-assisted review.

**Concern:** Thanks for expanding the lifecycle tests across `replay_screenshot_capture_test.dart`, `posthog_widget_test.dart`, and `native_occlusion_episode_test.dart`! Alongside the two `PostHogWidget` regression tests noted on `posthog_widget.dart`, a few new paths and cleanup details are still uncovered:

1. **`_startRecording()` while backgrounded (`posthog_widget.dart:284-287`):** `posthog_widget_test.dart:134-144` only sets `sessionRecordingActive.value = true` after returning to `resumed`. Consider adding a test that enables recording while `paused`/`inactive` and verifies `debugChangeDetectorRunning` stays `false` until `AppLifecycleState.resumed`.
2. **Post-`endOfFrame` lifecycle guards (`screenshot_capturer.dart:770, 870, 902, 926`) & static-screen `reset()` recovery:** None of the newly added post-`endOfFrame` guards are exercised yet, and `posthog_widget_test.dart` only checks `debugChangeDetectorRunning` rather than verifying that a static screen actually sends `sendMetaEvent` + `sendFullSnapshot` after resuming (including after `Posthog().reset()` while `inactive`).
3. **iOS coverage (`replay_screenshot_capture_test.dart:110-211`):** The new lifecycle tests currently use `TargetPlatformVariant.only(TargetPlatform.android)` even though `_canCaptureInCurrentLifecycle` applies to iOS as well — consider using `TargetPlatformVariant({TargetPlatform.android, TargetPlatform.iOS})`.
4. **Failure-path teardown hygiene:** All tests pass today, but `native_occlusion_episode_test.dart:665-678` (missing `try/finally` around `paused` → `resumed` and missing `await unmountAndFlush(tester)`) and `posthog_widget_test.dart:107-144` (resetting lifecycle only at the end in `unmount()`) would leak a non-`resumed` `lifecycleState` into later tests if an assertion fails mid-test. Moving `handleAppLifecycleStateChanged(AppLifecycleState.resumed)` into `try/finally` or `tearDown` prevents cross-test contamination.

AI-assisted review.

comments.body:
Thanks, good catch on the change detector. Pushed a follow-up commit: `PostHogWidgetState` is now a `WidgetsBindingObserver` that stops the `ChangeDetector` and cancels in-flight captures on inactive/hidden/paused/detached, and restarts it on resume (forcing a first frame, so static screens still get one). The capturer also re-checks the lifecycle before native view capture and before `toImage`/`toByteData`. Tests now cover paused/hidden/detached for both the capturer and the detector, plus an assertion in the in-flight test that the capture got past the entry guard. I also added the test you suggested: the lifecycle moves to paused inside the `getSessionReplayState` handler, and the capture returns null through the guard after the await (it hangs/fails when that guard is removed). As you asked, the occlusion placeholder stays outside the lifecycle gate: the check sits at the two capture call sites rather than in `_getImageBytes`, and a test builds the placeholder while paused.
On the AI policy question: this was written with an AI assistant (Claude Code) and checked with the unit/widget tests (full `flutter test` passes); I have not run it on an Android 15 device/emulator, so the GLES crash itself is not confirmed fixed on hardware. I've updated the PR description accordingly.

I reviewed the code myself.

Thanks for the detailed repros. Lifecycle cancellation now applies only to Flutter screenshots, and resume defers a fresh sample when an earlier capture is still in flight. I also applied the combined cancellation and lifecycle guard after the asynchronous capture stages and before each native view composite. The added widget tests cover the two reported races, recording enabled while paused, static recovery after an inactive reset, and a transition during native screenshot capture. All three test files pass locally, and the two race tests fail without this change.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
